A.title: GSE190905: paired change depends on resolution
A.poster_caption: Six donors contribute paired pre/post-radiotherapy measurements with explicit assignment coverage. Receptor change exceeds RFU change, while weighting, sampling and dominant-receptor removal affect the estimates.
A.manuscript_legend: Frozen GSE190905 pre/post comparisons from the cached six-donor release. Top: Receptor TV (nucleotide CDR3/V/J) and receptor functional unit (RFU) TV within the same threshold-qualified primary-TRB cells, with total, CD4 and CD8 subsets shown separately; lines connect one donor and black bars show equal-donor medians. TV denotes total variation. Coverage uses all 27,655 primary-TRB-bearing cells as denominator; 21,657 qualify at score 0.6 across twelve visits. All six donors meet the unchanged 100-qualified-cell-per-visit rule for these three subsets; other source-state strata have uneven support retained in A_support.tsv. Bottom: paired assignment coverage and RFU-TV sensitivities using cell weights, unique-receptor weights, within-donor medians of 50 existing without-replacement depth draws (500 cells except the 404-cell smaller visit of one donor), and removal of the union of each endpoint's dominant primary-TRB identity. Sensitivity lines pair donors; technical draw ranges are retained in the source table. Readout changes are descriptive, not a causal radiation comparison or evidence of preserved antigen function. The cached six-donor release is not the final seven-donor publication cohort. The manuscript assembly retains the three top comparisons; coverage and sensitivity remain in the standalone figure.
A.take_home: Paired repertoire measurements remain conditional on assignment coverage, sampling and clone weighting.
A.recommended_use: Main manuscript application; poster quantitative block.

B.title: GSE280982: change across the treatment timeline
B.poster_caption: Qualified-cell coverage and repertoire measurements retain the pre-treatment, last-radiation-day and six-week visit order. Missing visits remain unavailable; apparent RFU persistence need not retain the same observed receptors.
B.manuscript_legend: Completed GSE280982 external radiotherapy measurements. The visit grid displays qualified/primary-TRB cell counts and colors the qualified fraction among gene-expression (GEX)-matched primary-TRB cells; unavailable samples are hatched and explicitly marked missing, including HP01's unavailable tumor visits. Visits are categorical pre-treatment (P), last radiation day (R) and six weeks (6w), not a continuous time scale. Eleven supported visits contain 13,077 matched primary-TRB cells, of which 9,827 qualify; the unchanged rule is at least 100 qualified cells per visit. The three radiation-day tumor visits contain only 113, 143 and 157 qualified cells. Eight supported donor/tissue/interval pairs show Receptor TV (nucleotide CDR3/V/J) versus RFU TV, where TV is total variation and RFU is receptor functional unit. Repeated intervals reuse donors and are not independent participants. Persistence displays both persistent RFUs / union detected RFUs and persistent RFUs without a shared observed receptor / persistent RFUs at one-cell detection in both endpoints. Five-cell sensitivity, including zero-persistence undefined fractions, is preserved separately in B_persistence.tsv. No missing value is converted to zero. No source cell-state taxonomy was reconstructed and no causal treatment effect, absolute depletion or preserved antigen function is inferred. The compact manuscript assembly retains the visit grid and TV comparisons; the standalone figure also displays persistence.
B.take_home: Timeline and depth are essential context for interpreting the external repertoire measurements.
B.recommended_use: Main manuscript external application; poster quantitative block.

C.title: Common measurements, distinct sampling units
C.poster_caption: Frozen receptor/RFU total variation and aggregation cancellation are shown separately for RP1-14, GSE190905 and GSE280982. These are transportability examples with different units, intervals and reused donors, not a pooled treatment effect or biological replication.
C.manuscript_legend: Direct visualization of the frozen cross_application_summary.tsv, without recomputing any RP1-14 endpoint. Each row is an already-reported equal-donor median within a dataset, compartment and interval, or the observed value where n=1; donor counts are explicit. Receptor TV (nucleotide CDR3/V/J), receptor functional unit (RFU) TV and aggregation cancellation use the same within-study qualified universe; TV means total variation, and cancellation is summarized from donor-level differences rather than subtracted compartment medians. RP1-14 uses sequencing-read weights over 14.95–24.86 years; GSE190905 uses primary-TRB-cell weights pre/post radiotherapy; GSE280982 uses GEX-matched primary-TRB cells over pre-treatment, last radiation day and six weeks. RP1-14 CD4/CD8 rows reuse the same six donors and GSE280982 intervals reuse the same donors. No results are pooled, no effect-size ranking across incompatible biological settings is inferred, and no confidence interval or biological replication claim is attached. Persistence thresholds and coverage denominators differ and remain explicit in the source table; those fractions are not harmonized or pooled here.
C.take_home: The measurement framework transfers across datasets while sampling units and interpretation remain study-specific.
C.recommended_use: Manuscript cross-application synthesis; optional poster comparison.

D.title: Regulatory evidence at shared variants
D.poster_caption: Among 623 RFU-QTL variants, 17 overlap conditional expression-QTL selections and 32 overlap conditional chromatin-accessibility-QTL selections; six variants overlap both layers. The matrix retains TCR and non-TCR target labels and shows association evidence, not a causal mechanism or formal colocalization.
D.manuscript_legend: Completed Matos/RfuWAS regulatory evidence, restricted to the frozen report. Counts denote unique RFU-QTL variants: 623 published variants, 17 with source conditional eQTL selection, 32 with source conditional caQTL selection and six with both layers at the identical variant. The latter are included in both 17 and 32, so these counts are not disjoint. RFU denotes receptor functional unit, QTL quantitative trait locus, eQTL expression QTL, caQTL chromatin-accessibility QTL, and TCR T-cell receptor. Rows of the evidence matrix are the six same-variant overlaps, displaying the exact GRCh38 identity, conditional expression target and its frozen TCR/non-TCR class, number of distinct conditional chromatin target/rank records and associated RFUs. Molecular records are deduplicated across repeated variant–RFU joins; the six variants contribute six eQTL and ten caQTL target/rank records, 62 variant–RFU pairs and 36 RFUs in union. Exact peak identifiers, ranks and source statistics are retained in D_target_records.tsv. The non-TCR target ENSG00000289938 remains labeled non-TCR; this does not establish a non-TCR mechanism. Same-variant association and within-target conditional selection do not establish LD-independent mechanisms, mediation or formal RFU colocalization. No QTL search, reference check or model fit was repeated, and no genetic shortlist is intersected with radiotherapy outcomes.
D.take_home: Six exact shared variants support traceable regulatory follow-up, without establishing causality or colocalization.
D.recommended_use: Poster evidence panel; supporting manuscript figure, outside causal claims.

E.title: RFU addition did not improve held-out log loss
E.poster_caption: Across six held-out donors, adding RFU categories worsened clone-weighted mean log loss in both the ordinary and stricter purged designs. Positive delta explicitly means worse performance; this is a bounded negative result for the frozen benchmark.
E.manuscript_legend: Frozen, already-audited GSE190905 held-out prediction benchmark. Each of six donors is evaluated under ordinary donor generalization and a stricter design that removes training amino-acid CDR3/V/J identities shared with the held-out donor. The baseline uses TRBV, TRBJ and CDR3 length; the extended model adds receptor functional unit (RFU) categories. Left: baseline versus baseline+RFU clone-weighted log loss, with paired donor trajectories. Right: per-donor delta = extended minus baseline log loss; positive values mean worse prediction. Equal-donor means are 1.850996 versus 1.855212 (ordinary, delta +0.004216) and 1.852679 versus 1.856996 (purged, delta +0.004317). All six clone-weighted deltas are positive in each design. Cell-weighted sensitivities remain available in E_all_weightings.tsv, with no pooling across designs or cells. Donor aliases use the existing source crosswalk. Fixed models, training-only category support rules and source expression labels are unchanged; source TCR-gene exclusion from expression-feature selection is undocumented. No models or saved probabilities were refit/rescored. The result does not establish a universal absence of RFU–state relationships and does not invalidate longitudinal measurement utility.
E.take_home: The two frozen held-out designs show no RFU-added prediction gain.
E.recommended_use: Manuscript supplement; optional poster/Q&A backup only.

F.title: Wells: atlas coverage and source-label context
F.poster_caption: The atlas contains 610,429 cells from 24 donors, with 303,088 primary-TRB cells and 233,913 threshold-qualified cells. RFU support is summarized across tissues and source cell-type labels without claiming cell-state specificity.
F.manuscript_legend: Completed Wells public-atlas portability/context summaries. All 24 atlas donors remain in the denominator, including three with no eligible primary TRB; 21 donors contribute 303,088 primary-TRB cells across ten tissues, and 233,913 cells qualify at the frozen 0.6 threshold, representing 4,928 receptor functional units (RFUs). The donor–tissue grid shows qualified / primary-TRB coverage where primary TRB is observed; crosses denote an atlas sample with zero primary TRB, while blank gray cells indicate no atlas donor–tissue sample in the frozen coverage table. Undefined coverage is not assigned zero. Tissue bars separate primary-TRB and qualified counts. RFU breadth distributions count the number of tissues or distinct original cell_type labels with at least one qualified cell for each RFU; these are detection/support summaries, not specificity tests. A fixed public-data support rule of at least 50 qualified cells across four donors retains 1,471 RFUs, checked directly against the completed support table. All 17 source cell-type labels are retained in the source summary, including annotations outside conventional alpha-beta T-cell categories; they are neither relabeled nor interpreted as a new taxonomy. No attribution to largely unannotated cell_state values, survivor outcomes or causal function is made. No atlas assignment was rerun.
F.take_home: RFU portability is documented with donor, tissue and annotation denominators kept visible.
F.recommended_use: Manuscript context/supporting figure or supplement; optional poster panel.

poster_block.title: scRFU: quantitative evidence across applications
poster_block.poster_caption: Data-only GSE190905, GSE280982 and regulatory evidence panels are combined with deliberately unmarked space for BioRender artwork. These panels describe separate applications and do not establish a shared causal pathway.
poster_block.manuscript_legend: Poster quantitative block assembled from A, B and D using the same source tables and plotting functions. The lower-right region is deliberately blank; its normalized coordinates are recorded in the export manifest for later artwork placement. No conceptual workflow graphic, schematic receptor example or causal arrow is included. Native size is 762 × 609.6 mm with a minimum 18-point font; reducing the block also reduces label size. Statistical definitions, missingness, units and limitations are those of the individual panel legends.
poster_block.take_home: Quantitative panels can be reused beside manually authored artwork without joining distinct evidence into a causal story.
poster_block.recommended_use: APBC poster block, with reserved BioRender space.

manuscript_assembly.title: scRFU measurements across longitudinal applications
manuscript_assembly.poster_caption: Compact GSE190905 and GSE280982 panels accompany the separated cross-dataset comparison. Every value comes from a completed source table.
manuscript_assembly.manuscript_legend: Data-only cross-application assembly. A, GSE190905 paired receptor/RFU total variation in total, CD4 and CD8 subsets, with six supported donors per subset. B, GSE280982 ordered visit coverage and supported donor/tissue/interval TV comparisons, with missing visits displayed explicitly. C, frozen study-specific receptor/RFU TV and cancellation summaries for RP1-14, GSE190905 and GSE280982, preserving units and donor counts. The fuller standalone A/B figures provide sensitivity and persistence details. Regulatory evidence, the negative prediction benchmark and Wells context remain separate supporting panels D/E/F. No effects are pooled and no biological analyses or models are rerun.
manuscript_assembly.take_home: Common repertoire measurements can be presented together while preserving their study-specific denominators.
